title: 👑 Elite Challenge ⭐⭐⭐⭐: Master of the World Map

questions.prompt: Three of these sentences are correct. Which one is NOT correct?

options.text: I saw a cape in the shop.
I met a Indian in the train.
I saw an amphitheatre in Rome.
I visited the pyramids of Egypt.

questions.explanation: The faulty sentence is I met a Indian in the train: the word Indian begins with the vowel i, so it needs an. The three other sentences follow the same rule from the other side, with a before the consonant of cape, an before the vowel of amphitheatre, and the before pyramids that everybody already knows.

questions.prompt: The unit names five monuments. Which sentence about the Great Wall of China is correct?

options.text: The Great Wall is longer of the five.
The Great Wall is longest of the five.
The Great Wall is the longer of the five.
The Great Wall is the longest of the five.

questions.explanation: Five monuments make a whole group, and the first place of a group needs both ends of the tool: the in front and -est behind, so the Great Wall is the longest of the five. The ending -er belongs to two things compared, and the superlative never drops its the.

options.text: How about travel by plane to Spain?
How about travelling by plane in Spain?
How about travelling by plane to Spain?
Let's travelling by plane to Spain?

questions.explanation: Three rules meet here: after How about the verb takes -ing, the plane is a vehicle so it takes by, and Spain is a place so it takes to. Each of the other sentences breaks exactly one of them, with the bare travel, the preposition in in front of the country, or the -ing form after Let's, which always wants the bare verb.

questions.prompt: Read: "Big Ben was finished in 1859, the Eiffel Tower in 1889, and the amphitheatre of El Jem was built about 1800 years ago." Which sentence is true?

options.text: Big Ben is older than the Eiffel Tower.
Big Ben is the oldest of the three.
The Eiffel Tower is older than Big Ben.
The amphitheatre of El Jem is the newest of the three.

questions.explanation: 1859 comes before 1889, so Big Ben is older than the Eiffel Tower, and two monuments compared take the ending -er with than. Big Ben is not the oldest of the group, because the amphitheatre of El Jem is about 1800 years old, which also makes it the oldest and not the newest of the three.

questions.prompt: Which sentence describes a custom of Spain correctly?

options.text: In Spain, people are eating paella.
In Spain, people ate paella.
In Spain, people eat paella.
In Spain, people will eat paella.

questions.explanation: A custom is what people do again and again, year after year, so it is told in the simple present: In Spain, people eat paella. The form are eating describes this minute only, ate puts the custom in a finished past, and will eat sends it to a day that has not come yet.

questions.prompt: Read: "Karim lives in Tunis. First he travels to Gabes, in the south of the country, and then to Tabarka, in the north-west." In which direction does Karim travel first?

options.text: east
north
north-west
south

questions.explanation: The text says he goes first to Gabes, which is in the south of the country, so his first journey takes him south. The direction north-west is the second one, towards Tabarka, and neither north alone nor east is named anywhere in the text.
